Assays with activity are indicated by bold type. For NADH oxidation each 1-ml assay mixture incubated at 25°C contained 50 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 0.1 mM NADH, 0.1 mM crotonyl-CoA, 5 μM FAD, 2 mM DTT, 0.01 mg purified butyryl-CoA dehydrogenase/Etf complex, and, where indicated, 20 μM ferredoxin (Fd), 0.4 U hydrogenase (Hyd) from C. pasteurianum, and/or 1 mM methyl viologen. For TTC reduction each 1-ml assay mixture incubated at 25°C contained 50 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 0.2 mM NADH, 0.1 mM crotonyl-CoA, 5 μM FAD, 0.4 mM TTC, 2 mM DTT, 0.01 mg purified butyryl-CoA dehydrogenase/Etf complex, and, where indicated, 20 μM ferredoxin. For ferredoxin reduction each 0.5-ml assay mixture incubated at 37°C contained 50 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 2 mM DTT, 2.5 mM NADH, 1 mM crotonyl-CoA, 10 μM FAD, 0.05 mg purified butyryl-CoA dehydrogenase/Etf complex, and, where indicated, 50 μM ferredoxin, 1.6 U hydrogenase from C. pasteurianum, and/or 1 mM methyl viologen. The reactions were started by addition of crotonyl-CoA. One unit was equivalent to 1 μmol of NADH oxidized per min, 1 μmol of TTC reduced per min, or 1 μmol of H2 formed per min.

(i) H2 formation assay.
Ferredoxin reduction catalyzed by the butyryl-CoA dehydrogenase/Etf complex was assayed by coupling this reaction with the hydrogenase reaction (reaction 6). Using 0.5- or 1-ml mixtures, the assays were performed at 37°C in 6.5-ml serum bottles closed with a rubber stopper and filled with N2 at a pressure of 1.2 × 105 Pa. (For the compositions of the assay mixtures, see Tables 1 and 2.) The gas phase and the liquid phase were equilibrated by continuous shaking. After the reaction was started, 0.2-ml gas samples were withdrawn at 1-min intervals and assayed for H2 by gas chromatography. One unit was defined as the formation of 1 μmol H2 per min.

Both the absolute and relative values of the specific activities varied from preparation to preparation. This was not only because the enzyme complex was very labile but also because there were inherent difficulties with the activity measurements. Some of the reactions started with a considerable lag period, and the rates of the reactions were not always proportional to the amounts of enzyme added.
